map_disagreements.why: The single most valuable disagreement in this deck. Six cards read the SAME input - an opponent drew a card, or cast a spell - and each states a different OUTPUT, so the map, which is built from card text, files them by what they produce. Smothering Tithe reads as ramp because it says Treasure. Heliod reads as a creature because his type line is one. Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Consecrated Sphinx and Faerie Mastermind read as draw. No card in the group says what the group is for, so this layer is invisible in card text and cannot be seen by a reader looking at the constellation. The run makes the case for grouping them: 2,322 trigger lines off one shared event.

26 cards across five cities - the map splits them by HOW they answer (counter text, destroy text, a body, a Treasure rider on An Offer You Can't Refuse) while the deck uses all of them for one job: buy turns until you can cast a seven-drop twice. Kefnet the Mindful lands in Card Flow because his activated ability draws, which is the least important thing he does here.

Pearl Medallion and Sapphire Medallion are cost reduction, not production, so the map puts them with the white spells and the X-creatures rather than with the rocks. In this deck they do the rocks' job - shave the bill on a colour-heavy curve. goldfish_targets does NOT count them, in any of its eleven targets' need groups (`grep -c Medallion data/decks/heliod/goldfish_targets.json` returns 0): they were in "Heliod plus the mana to flip him" until c879dcd removed them, because a spell-cost reducer cannot pay any part of "{3}{U/P}: Transform Heliod", an activated ability, and neither card taps for mana. The any_of now holds six members and the live figures are 0.732 assembled, 0.554 by turn six, mean turn 4.852.

Nine of eleven cluster cleanly, which is unusual. The two strays are structural rather than semantic: Mikokoro is a land and its text is mostly a mana ability, and Enlightened Tutor is a search, so it sits with the other tutors regardless of what it fetches in this 99.

No disagreement, but the address is worth naming: Approach sits in Card Flow with the draw engine - the map read it on 'gain 7 life' and 'seventh from the top' - while Mystical Tutor and Long-Term Plans, the only two cards that find it, sit in Bodies. The deck's win and its route to the win have different addresses.

open_questions.question: Can the goldfish measure the card side of this deck - Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Kefnet, Alhammarret's Archive, Teferi's Ageless Insight, Psychosis Crawler, Kwain and Loran are all in `draw_not_modelled` - so that a claim about whether mana or cards binds this deck has both arms measured?
open_questions.why_it_matters: meta.card_advantage reports 13 cards that draw against 2 modelled. Forge now says the unmodelled half is where the deck lives: 2,322 conversion triggers and 851 drain resolutions over 120 games, none of it visible to the goldfish. Until that channel is modelled, the mana stage can only say mana is a MEASURED constraint, not that it is the binding one.

open_questions.question: Should the gift and fort components be scored on a card being ON THE BATTLEFIELD, or on it having been USED? Loran of the Third Path was cast in 32 of 120 Forge games and its draw ability was activated zero times; Temple Bell was cast in 22 and activated 64 times.
open_questions.why_it_matters: 'Table draw engine online' assembles 0.92 and is the figure every other stage leans on, but it prices DRAWING one of eleven cards. Two of the eleven (Mikokoro, Temple Bell) and two more (Kwain, Loran) need an activation the deck must have spare mana for, and the repo's own Ashnod's Altar precedent is that a Forge AI may simply never use an outlet with no board payoff. If the assembled rate is really an upper bound, it is an upper bound on the deck's single most-cited number.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Scrawling Crawler to the FIRST any_of (the ten-card gift group). It is already in the first any_of of "Table draw engine online" and in the second any_of of this target, so the same file calls it a table draw engine in one target and not in the other.
proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Table draw engine plus a draw-triggered drain, both drawn
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Scrawling Crawler is both halves of this label in one card: "At the beginning of your upkeep, each player draws a card" is the table draw engine, and "Whenever an opponent draws a card, that player loses 1 life" is the draw-triggered drain (oracle text, cards.json). As written the target cannot assemble on it alone - the first group lists Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran, The Second Doctor and Forced Fruition, and Scrawling Crawler is not among them - so a hand holding the one card that does the whole job scores as half of it. RECEIPT, RUN: `grep -c "Scrawling Crawler" data/decks/heliod/goldfish_targets.json` returns 4 and `grep -n` puts them at line 18 (first any_of of "Table draw engine online"), line 42 (inside this target's own label, not a member), line 47 (the Crawler any_of) and line 72 (this target's SECOND any_of); the first any_of of this target spans lines 56-67 and holds exactly ten names. This target is the deck's lowest at 0.328 assembled and 0.196 by turn six, and lines[4] rests on it - and Forge says this card carried the whole drain axis (851 of 865 resolutions), so the direction of the error matters before the figure is read as a weakness.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Split it, or add a second target that requires Approach of the Second Sun itself rather than any_of three cards - and if the harness can express it, gate on a second cast rather than on drawing the card.
proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Win condition access (Approach, or a tutor that can actually find a sorcery)
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The n120 run separates two things this target merges. Approach was cast at all in 27 of 120 Forge games; a SECOND cast happened in 12, and all 12 were wins. The declared target scores 0.495 assembled because it fires on Mystical Tutor or Long-Term Plans being DRAWN, neither of which is the win - Long-Term Plans does not appear anywhere in the run's logs. As written the deck's most-cited access figure is roughly double the rate at which the thing it stands for actually happened. I cannot tell whether goldfish.py's `_target_met` can express a repeat cast or a mana condition, which is why this is a proposal and open_questions[3] is a question.

stages.label: WHAT PAYS FOR {6}{W} TWICE
stages.what_it_does:
32 of the deck's 33 land copies sit here in 17 entries (Mikokoro is placed in ignition), plus eight rocks and cost-reducers. The bill this stage exists to pay is Approach's, twice: {6}{W} is seven mana on two separate turns. goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn crosses 7 between turn 8 (6.966) and turn 9 (7.612), and that is with the commander's discount switched OFF - model-coverage gives Heliod only the `bodies` channel.

Measured on the CURRENT list. benchmark missed_land_drop_rate 0.2532, worst turn six; land_drop_hit_rate 0.729 / 0.603 / 0.540 across turns four to six. mana_analysis.json (sha 214af3084f80) gives 25 W and 26 U total sources against a Karsten 90%-on-curve figure of 36 each, and that file's own note calls the target "a yardstick, not a possibility, in a 33-land deck". Lands-only on-curve 0.610 W / 0.639 U, and 0.580 / 0.610 with Skycloud Expanse set aside as the one gated source. deck-audit reads mana-base and colour-sources UNDER for archetype control. In the n120 run heliod played a mean 8.42 lands (median 8.0); the record's piloting block gives lands_ratio 1.049, so our seat developed mana about as well as the pod did.

Second jobs. Pearl and Sapphire Medallion reduce the cost of white and blue SPELLS rather than produce mana, which is why the map files them away from the rocks and why they cannot pay any part of the commander's flip; see map_disagreements[2]. Reliquary Tower, Decanter of Endless Water and Thought Vessel each carry "You have no maximum hand size", the clause Kefnet and Psychosis Crawler both read. Adarkar Wastes is also this deck's largest source of damage to ITSELF - 83 of the 128 points in stages[4].

stages.label: THE GIFT - THE TABLE STARTS DRAWING
stages.what_it_does:
The first thing that has to happen, and the cheapest. EIGHT of the ten permanents here hand the WHOLE table cards - Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and The Second Doctor all say "each player". Two do not: Loran of the Third Path is "you and TARGET OPPONENT each draw a card", and Forced Fruition draws seven to the opponent who cast a spell. The resource every later stage reads - a card an opponent drew this turn - does not exist until one of these resolves. Enlightened Tutor draws nobody; it is here because it finds five of the ten - Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell, Dictate of Kruphix, Forced Fruition, artifact or enchantment only - and cannot find Approach.

THE GIFT IS THE PART OF THIS ENGINE FORGE ACTUALLY RAN. All five triggered pieces, heliod-controlled trigger lines across the n120 run: Dictate of Kruphix 577, Forced Fruition 339, Howling Mine 300, Font of Mythos 184, Kami of the Crescent Moon 125, The Second Doctor 84. Activations: Temple Bell 64, Kwain 46, Mikokoro 26. ONE PIECE NEVER FIRED - Loran of the Third Path was cast in 32 of 120 games and its "{T}: You and target opponent each draw a card" appears in ZERO activated lines (open_questions[6]).

The rate belongs to the declared component, not to this stage. "Table draw engine online" assembles in 0.92 of goldfish games (0.97 with tutors), 0.828 by turn six, mean turn 2.461 - enumerated across all eleven declared targets, the highest assembled_rate (next 0.843) and the lowest mean turn (next 2.819). Its eleven members are these ten plus Scrawling Crawler, MINUS Enlightened Tutor. Mikokoro is counted here rather than in mana for its "{2}, {T}: Each player draws a card".

stages.label: YOUR OWN CARD FLOW, AND THE ONLY ROUTE BACK
stages.what_it_does:
What keeps the deck running once the table is drawing: eight cards that turn mana into cards for you, plus the two tutors that can actually find the win.

Alhammarret's Archive and Teferi's Ageless Insight each read "if you would draw a card except the first one you draw in each of YOUR draw steps, draw two cards instead" - `your` is the load-bearing word in a deck whose gift fires in every player's draw step. Both are live in Forge: that replacement effect fired 349 times across the n120 run, with the Archive cast in 32 games and the Insight in 17. The declared component "Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine" (0.787 assembled, 0.581 by turn six) groups them with Rhystic Study and Consecrated Sphinx; they are split out here because they read YOUR draws, a different trigger and a different job. Of the five X-draw spells, TWO - Prosperity and Skyscribing - draw the whole table; Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius and Mathemagics each target one player and feed the same turn's discount only when aimed at an opponent. Dig Through Time delves, so its printed eight overstates what you pay.

ENUMERATED, because the role tag says otherwise: of the 99, only Mystical Tutor (instant or sorcery) and Long-Term Plans (any card, third from the top) can find Approach of the Second Sun. Enlightened Tutor is artifact-or-enchantment. Drift of Phantasms transmutes for mana value 3; Approach is 7. The declared "Win condition access" component is those two plus Approach itself and assembles 0.495 (0.677 with tutors), 0.361 by turn six. Forge found the route: Mystical Tutor was cast in 38 of 120 games. Long-Term Plans does not appear in the run's logs at all, in any line kind.

cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

deck-facts roles: Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind and Smothering Tithe all carry draw:engine, but so do Arcane Denial, Psychosis Crawler, Scrawling Crawler and The Second Doctor - the role does not separate a converter from a draw spell

stages.label: THE ASYMMETRY LAYER - SIX CARDS, ONE TRIGGER
stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper. The gift is symmetric and therefore not card advantage; these six make it one-sided, reading one event and paying it out in different currencies. Consecrated Sphinx draws two on every opponent draw; Faerie Mastermind one on each opponent's second; Smothering Tithe makes a Treasure unless they pay {2}; Rhystic Study and Mystic Remora bill casts, not draws.

THIS LAYER RAN. Heliod-controlled trigger lines over the n120 run: Smothering Tithe 998, Mystic Remora 511, Rhystic Study 410, Consecrated Sphinx 326, Faerie Mastermind 77 - 2,322 from five cards cast in 24 to 39 games each.

THE COMMANDER IS TWO CARDS AND ONLY THE BACK ONE DOES THIS STAGE'S JOB. Heliod, the Warped Eclipse is "You may cast spells as though they had flash" and "Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn". The front face is a {2}{W}{W} body whose ETB recurs an enchantment; the flip is a sorcery-speed "{3}{U/P}". He RESOLVED in 68 of 120 games (0.567 [0.477, 0.652]) and TRANSFORMED in 35 (0.292 [0.218, 0.378]), median first flip global turn 36. The multiplier this stage is named for was live in 35 games, not 68.

THE FLIP CROSS-TAB DID NOT REPLICATE. On this run the 35 flip games hold 6 wins (0.171) and the 85 no-flip games hold 14 (0.165) - flat. The previous model read 0.114 against 0.271 on the v1.0.0 run; that did not hold, and neither run could resolve a gap that size. What survives both: the wins do not WAIT on the flip - 10 of the 12 Approach wins are no-flip games, and the gift assembles at 0.92, mean player-turn 2.461. Multiplier, not ignition.

No `fodder` stage: nothing here is converted by being spent. The resource this engine eats is manufactured on the opponents' side of the table.

stages.label: WHAT IT PRODUCES - AND THE METRIC THAT CANNOT SEE IT
stages.what_it_does:
THE DRAIN IS LIFE LOSS, NOT DAMAGE, AND THAT CHANGES THE VERDICT THE PREVIOUS MODEL WROTE. Psychosis Crawler is "whenever you draw a card, each opponent loses 1 life"; Scrawling Crawler is "whenever an opponent draws a card, that player loses 1 life". Neither is damage, so `noncombat_damage_dealt_to_players` cannot see either at any value - reading that field as this axis's verdict was the previous model's largest measurement error.

COUNTED FROM THE RUN'S LOGS. "Whenever an opponent draws a card, that player loses 1 life" resolved 851 times (giada-angels 378, baylen-tokens 237, abaddon 236) and "whenever you draw a card, each opponent loses 1 life" 14 times, three opponents each. That is 893 life over 120 games: mean 7.44, MEDIAN 0.0, nonzero in 47, max 104. Scrawling Crawler, cast in 46 games, is essentially the whole of it. Read the pair: off in most games, enormous in a few - a spread, not a clock.

WHAT THE DAMAGE FIELD ACTUALLY HOLDS. heliod's `noncombat_damage_dealt_to_players` sums to 148 (mean 1.23, median 0.0, max 10, nonzero in 48). Splitting the logs by target seat: 128 of those points are heliod damaging its OWN seat - Adarkar Wastes 83, Talisman of Progress 43, 2 more - and only 20 reach an opponent, every one of them Walking Ballista. The metric is not split by whether the target is an opponent; quote it only with that clause attached.

The rest. Four X-cards leave a permanent behind: Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker, Mikaeus the Lunarch; Ballista was cast in 52 games and activated 99 times, the most-activated card in the deck. Combat: mean 3.28 dealt, MEDIAN 0.5; commander damage reached 21 in ZERO games. The declared two-card component assembles 0.366, 0.256 by turn six.

The arithmetic is 26 - 20, not 26 - 21: only 20 of the deck's 21 answer cards sit here, because Walking Ballista carries the deck's ONLY removal:damage and this model files it in output. benchmark and this model therefore disagree about one card, and the 6-of-15 class coverage is benchmark's, not this stage's.

The 30-of-32 figure, enumerated rather than recalled. data/opponents/giada-angels/decklist.txt holds 31 creature entries plus the commander Giada, Font of Hope. Reading each one's oracle text from cards.csv: 30 carry flying on the body. Starnheim Aspirant ("Angel spells you cast cost {2} less to cast") has none, and BISHOP OF WINGS has no flying either - its only occurrence of the word is "create a 1/1 white Spirit creature token with flying", the text-match trap. strategic_frame.json states this as "31 of whose 32 creature cards carry flying ... the lone exception is Starnheim Aspirant" and misses Bishop of Wings too; the two artifacts disagree, and this is the enumerated one. The opponent seat is byte-identical across both runs (decklist_sha256 c322a589).

stages.label: THE 26 CARDS THAT BUY THE TURNS
stages.what_it_does:
26 of 85 entries, the largest stage; its job is to survive to a seven-drop cast twice. Four layers, and this is the FIRST run measured on a list that holds them - v1.1.0's insurance and v1.2.0's skies post-date the v1.0.0 run.

COUNTERS (8, two free). "Free or cheap interaction held" assembles 0.843, 0.707 by turn six, but interaction_castable is 0.626 at turn six against 0.927 in hand: holding it and paying for it are different problems. Forge cast a mean 0.79 a game.

REMOVAL (7), of which only Day of Judgment and Supreme Verdict are sweepers - two against a control target of 5-7, UNDER (notes[4]).

THE FORT (6): Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Archangel of Tithes tax attackers - 0.487 assembled, 0.355 by turn six, the least reliable defensive component. Angelic Wall, Drift of Phantasms, Kefnet and Archangel are four of the six-card flier-blocker component (Sphinx and Faerie Mastermind sit in conversion), 0.750; Kefnet cannot block under seven cards in hand.

INSURANCE (5), Leyline of Anticipation included because it duplicates the flash grant without him - 0.680 assembled, 0.526 by turn six. Two of the five are unmeasured in Forge: neither Guardian of Faith nor Teferi's Protection has a cast line anywhere in the logs (notes[6]); Lightning Greaves was cast in 29 games, activated 41 times.

THE AIR, RE-MEASURED. heliod was eliminated in 74 of 120 games and `eliminated_how` records only {damage: 61}, so 13 deaths have no attributed killer - unknown, not non-damage. Of the 61, `eliminated_by` gives giada-angels 43, abaddon 11, baylen-tokens 7 - the pre-fort run's picture (39 of 53) on a list that now blocks and taxes. Combat damage taken mean 37.92, median 30.5. The fort's premise holds (evidence[2]); this run does not show it changing who kills us.

evidence.id: Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor
evidence.note: the single contained Commander Spellbook line, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 15, produces 'Win the game'; it is a candidate, and stack 002 is what makes this one a fact

Approach carries the deck's only wincon:alt role (deck-facts histogram: wincon:alt 1). The single_point_of_failure field is AUTHORED and machine-read, so its qualifier belongs beside it: of heliod's 20 wins on the current list, 12 read won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'" and 8 read "all opponents have lost", so the deck closes without this card in 8 of 20. deck_audit's own engine.single_points_of_failure is [], because every declared component holds two or more members; this model asserts one anyway because the wincon stage genuinely holds one card - the only other win-flavoured roles in the 99 are the two wincon:drain Crawlers, which stages[4] measures at a median of 0.0 life a game. Read the field as "the only card that WINS", not "the only way the game ends".

stages.label: ONE CARD, AND IT IS 12 FOR 12
stages.what_it_does:
Approach of the Second Sun, cast twice from hand. The first cast gains 7 life and puts the card seventh from the top; the second wins outright.

THE BEST-EVIDENCED SENTENCE IN THIS MODEL. Counting `Add To Stack: ... cast Approach of the Second Sun` across the n120 run's logs: 39 casts in 27 of 120 games, and exactly 12 games reached a SECOND cast. Cross-tabbed against the record's `games[]`, those 12 are exactly the 12 marked won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'" - twelve for twelve. The other 15 games got one cast and none won on it. The deck's whole difficulty sits between the first cast and the second, not in the card resolving.

THE COLUMN. 20 wins, 12 by Approach and 8 by "all opponents have lost": win rate 0.202, ci95 [0.135, 0.292] over the 99 games with a winner. Twenty games clocked out and one was a draw, so 21 of 120 have no winner and are excluded. Against par for a four-player pod the difference is -0.050, ci95 [-0.155, +0.056]; against this table's measured null of 0.180 it is +0.017, ci95 [-0.083, +0.116]. Both SPAN ZERO - indistinguishable from both. Mean finishing position 2.628 over 94 ranked games (11 firsts, 35 seconds, 26 thirds, 22 fourths).

AND NOT THAT THE DECK GOT WORSE. v1.0.0 scored 27/108 (0.250), v1.2.1 scores 20/100 (0.200), and the Newcombe interval on the DIFFERENCE is [-0.1614, +0.0644], spanning zero. This pair of runs could only detect 0.185 at 80% power. Fifteen swaps produced a change this bench cannot measure - notes[0].

This is a ONE-finisher deck; the pilot's standing constraint against two-card infinites rules out the usual second route - deck-facts reads two_card_infinites 0 and bracket_report's list is empty. Stack 002 settles the skill and is quoted in evidence[0].

thesis: Heliod manufactures a resource nobody at the table prices - cards in your opponents' hands - converts it into a cost discount, one-sided draw, Treasure and life loss, and spends the turns that buys casting Approach of the Second Sun twice; the second cast is 12 for 12 and everything else is the wait.
